[DB-1] Serverless DB connection exhaustion risk
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: PrismaClient is instantiated at module load and the global cache is only set when NODE_ENV !== "production", and DATABASE_URL is passed directly with no pooler hints. This means production serverless instances will create new DB connections per cold start with no pooler.
Impact: On Vercel/other serverless, this will exhaust Postgres connections at small concurrency (~50-200 concurrent lambdas) causing total outage.

finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Serverless DB connection exhaustion risk
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: PrismaClient is instantiated at module load and the global cache is only set when NODE_ENV !== "production", and DATABASE_URL is passed directly with no pooler hints. This means production serverless instances will create new DB connections per cold start with no pooler.
Impact: On Vercel/other serverless, this will exhaust Postgres connections at small concurrency (~50-200 concurrent lambdas) causing total outage.  
Fix: Use a pooled DB proxy (PgBouncer/Neon pooler/Upstash pool) or configure Prisma to connect via a pooler and persist a singleton across instances (or use a connection-limited server runtime).

[DB-2] Coupon decrement + order creation not atomic (double-spend risk)
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Code reads coupon, checks quantity, then runs await prisma.coupon.update(...) to decrement before creating/updating the order, with no surrounding transaction or row locking. These steps are separate DB calls and can race.
Impact: Under concurrent checkout attempts the coupon quantity can be overspent (double-use) resulting in financial inconsistency at tens to low hundreds of concurrent checkouts.  
Fix: Wrap coupon validation+decrement and order creation in a single transaction (SELECT FOR UPDATE or transactional conditional update) so decrement and order creation are atomic.

[DB-3] Per-item DB round-trips when updating existing orders (N+1 writes)
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L220-L480)
Evidence: When an existing PENDING order is updated the code fetches existingOrderItems then loops typedItems performing individual prisma.orderItem.update/create/delete calls for each item (and deleteMany per old item). This issues multiple serial queries per item instead of a batched operation.  
Impact: With orders containing many items and moderate concurrency (hundreds of requests/sec), this multiplies DB queries and will quickly raise latency and connection usage, causing failures around hundreds of concurrent updates.  
Fix: Replace per-item serial updates with bulk operations (createMany/updateMany/deleteMany with batched IDs) or run all item mutations inside a single transaction with fewer round trips.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-4] Unbounded product list query (no pagination)
File: src/app/api/products/route.ts (L1-L140)
Evidence: products endpoint does prisma.product.findMany({ include: { colors: ... }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' } }) with no take/skip or cursor pagination.  
Impact: As products grow, this will return and scan the entire products table causing high latency and memory blowups on list endpoints at tens of thousands of rows.  
Fix: Add pagination (cursor or limit/offset) and a lightweight list projection to avoid full-table scans.

[DB-5] Missing indexes on high-traffic filters and ORDER BY columns
File: prisma/schema.prisma (L1-L400)
Evidence: OrderItem has no explicit index on orderId, Product has no index on createdAt, and Order.createdAt lacks an index while code does orderItem/findMany by orderId and product/orderBy createdAt and admin export orders orderBy createdAt.  
Impact: Table scans will appear once rows hit ~100k, slowing core flows (order lookups, product listing, CSV export) from ms to seconds and causing cascading request queues.  
Fix: Add indexes: @@index([orderId]) on OrderItem, @@index([createdAt]) on Product and Order (or targeted composite indexes matching common WHERE/ORDER BY patterns).

[DB-6] Reviews included inline for product page (unbounded payload)
File: src/app/api/products/[slug]/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: product.findUnique includes reviews: true and then computes average rating in app code, pulling the full reviews array into memory.  
Impact: Popular products with many reviews will produce huge responses and increased DB load; this will slow page loads and increase memory especially at scale.  
Fix: Replace include reviews with aggregate queries (count/avg) or limit the included reviews (pagination) and compute aggregates in DB.

[DB-7] Stock decrement race/oversell potential under concurrency
File: src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts (L1-L200) and src/app/api/checkout/confirm-order/route.ts (L1-L140)
Evidence: Both endpoints decrement product or productColor stock inside a transaction but do not assert stock >= quantity or re-check via conditional update (no SELECT FOR UPDATE or WHERE stock >= X).  
Impact: Concurrent confirmations can still cause oversell (negative stock) at mid-high concurrency (hundreds of confirmations of same SKU) leading to inventory inconsistencies and refunds.  
Fix: Use conditional updates that fail when stock insufficient (UPDATE ... SET stock = stock - n WHERE id = x AND stock >= n) inside the transaction and handle failure, or lock the row explicitly.

--- INFO ---

[DB-8] Prisma client global caching only in dev
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: globalForPrisma.prisma is assigned only when NODE_ENV !== "production".  
Use: This explains why production instances will create fresh PrismaClients per instance — relevant context for the connection exhaustion risk above.
